newsitem.title: CHINA: HK new airport signs business air centre franchise.
newsitem.headline: HK new airport signs business air centre franchise.

text.p: Hong Kong's Airport Authority said on Friday it had signed a franchise agreement for the operation of a business aviation centre at the new Chek Lap Kok airport.

The centre, to be completed by the end of 1998, would provide services for executive aircraft and passengers, including ground handling, baggage handling, refuelling, security and flight planning, the authority said in a statement.
Hong Kong Business Aviation Centre Ltd would hold the franchise for 15 years, it said.
The shareholders of the franchise are Sung Hung Kai Properties Ltd, the AMR Combs unit of AMR Corp, China Southern Airlines Co Ltd and tycoons Michael Kadoorie, Christopher Cheng and Henry Tang.
The initial investment is HK$68 million.
Chek Lap Kok is scheduled to open in April 1998 and will replace the existing Kai Tak airport.
